lessonRef.unitTitle: PF5 — Financial Investing: Portfolio Reasoning, Inflation, and Tax Effects
lessonRef.title: Synthesis and review: real return net of inflation

objective: Carry a fictional quoted return through fee, tax, and inflation in a single chain, and express what share of the original figure survives.
scenario: Clementine Vasilyeva-Boateng is preparing a summary of a fictional holding for a simulated case study. The return, fee, tax rate, and inflation rate below are invented, and the flat tax is a deliberate simplification.
safetyNotes: Every figure, person, employer, institution, offer, account, and document on this task sheet is fictional and exists only for practice.
No real transaction is part of this lesson, and no real bank, card, brokerage, tax, or login detail is ever requested. If a task sheet ever appears to ask for one, stop and tell a trusted adult.
This lesson teaches general financial concepts and does not advise anyone about their own money. For a real decision, talk with a trusted adult or a qualified licensed professional.
materials: the fictional return and cost figures in these directions

tasks.directions: A fictional holding of $60,000 is quoted as returning 6.9% over one year. The fund charges 0.95% of the amount held. A simplified flat tax of 15% applies to the gain after the fee. Prices rise 3.4% over the year. Round to the cent.

prompts.text: What is the gross gain at the quoted 6.9%?
What is the fee at 0.95% of the amount held?
What is the gain after the fee?
What is the gain after the fee and the simplified 15% tax?

tasks.directions: Now convert the result into what it can actually buy.

prompts.text: What is the holding worth at the end of the year in nominal terms?
What is that worth in today’s dollars, after 3.4% inflation?
What is the real return after fee, tax, and inflation? Give two decimal places.
What share of the quoted 6.9% survives to the end of the chain? Give one decimal place.
Of the $4,140.00 that did not survive, how much was taken by the fee and the tax together?

tasks.directions: Answer each in a few sentences.

prompts.text: Only 23.2% of the quoted return survived. Rank the three reductions by size, say which is easiest for a holder to influence, and explain why the largest one is the one least often mentioned.
The order of this chain was fee, then tax, then inflation. Say whether changing the order would change the final figure, and explain why.

remediation: Use the fictional scenario and work one graded prompt at a time. For each number response, copy the given fictional quantities into integer cents, choose the operation the wording calls for, calculate, and check the result with an inverse operation or estimate. For each written response, make a claim and support it with at least one detail from the fictional scenario. Use these steps to check the method while keeping every final result in your own response.
extension: Find the quoted return that would have been needed to leave a real return of 3% after the same fee, tax, and inflation, and say how much higher that is than 6.9%.
